subject: Agent sync interruption after private upgrade — recovery and next steps
messages:
From: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medicore.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T22:41:00Z
Subject: Issues after Private Agent upgrade — immediate help requested

Mina,

We saw a spike in 5xxs and an inability for our on-prem nodes to re-establish control-plane sync after the maintenance window this evening. The agents show repeated TLS handshake resets with the control-plane IPs and our side reports connection churn starting at 21:12 UTC. This impacted a small subset of customers on our cluster; we’ve fenced traffic but still need guidance on root cause and remediation steps.

I attached logs and the upgrade manifest. We can hop on a call if helpful.

Attachments: redwood-agent-logs-20270403.tar.gz (1.2MB), privatenet-upgrade-manifest-20270403.yaml (4KB)

Carlos Reyes
Director, Platform Ops
MediCore Health

- I’ll coordinate a short war room (30 min) for 02:00 UTC if that works for your on-call.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T02:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Issues after Private Agent upgrade — immediate help requested

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 02:09 Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Carlos — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating to our Private team.

Quick findings from initial triage:
- The agent logs show successful TCP connect attempts followed by TLS alerts with "unexpected_message" from the agent side; server side (control-plane) logs show "certificate verify failed" for a subset of agent certs.
- The upgrade applied a cert rotation step (thumbprint rotation) that we push as part of the 2027-04-03 manifest; it looks like agents with older pinned roots did not pick up the rotated CA bundle.
- We replicated in our lab by re-running the upgrade manifest against a staging agent; behaviour matched.

Actionable next steps (short window):
1) Advise MediCore to re-run agent bootstrap pointing at the new CA bundle (we can provide a single-line curl + install). This is lowest-risk and quick (estimated 6–8 minutes per node).
2) If they prefer, we can push a targeted rolling re-provision from the control-plane; this requires coordination and a brief traffic freeze per node.

Ben and I will draft the exact commands and a recovery runbook. Mina — happy to talk ops with Carlos on the call.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medicore.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Issues after Private Agent upgrade — immediate help requested

Carlos — thanks for staying on this. Below is the minimal recovery step we validated in staging; we recommend doing this during a low-traffic minute and monitoring the agent table for re-registers.

Recovery runbook (minimal):
1) On MediCore node: sudo systemctl stop redwood-agent
2) sudo mv /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem.old
3) curl -sS https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/ca/20270403/ca-bundle.pem -o /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem
4) sudo systemctl start redwood-agent
5) tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/agent.log | grep "registered" to confirm success

If you prefer we can run a rolling re-provision from our control plane (option B) — that requires a signed consent and a short maintenance window per host.

I’ve attached a concise PDF runbook: recovery-runbook-v1.pdf

Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medicore.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — TLS cert rotation impact

Carlos / Team — thank you for patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident note and committed follow-ups.

Summary:
- During the 2027-04-03 Private upgrade, our automated cert rotation step deployed an updated CA bundle. A subset of on-prem agents had pinned older root bundles and did not fetch the rotation, resulting in TLS verification failures and intermittent control-plane disconnects between ~21:12–22:05 UTC. Impact was restricted to ~12 nodes on your cluster; no customer data exposure identified.

Immediate remediation taken:
- Provided MediCore the quick re-bootstrap steps (Apr 4) to replace the CA bundle; your on-call confirmed re-registers for affected agents.
- We validated the rollback and a targeted control-plane reprovision option if you prefer vendor-assisted remediation.

Committed follow-ups (ownership):
- Redwood Private: implement pre-rotation compatibility check and a gated rollout flag (ETA 2027-05-01) — owner: Vivek Kulkarni.
- Product: add explicit opt-in for CA bundle rotation with customer notification and dry-run option (ETA 2027-06-01) — owner: Ben Carter.
- Account: Mina to coordinate a short exec briefing and credit review (if requested) — owner: Mina Haddad.

Attachments: recovery-runbook-v1.pdf; we’ve also uploaded full postmortem artifacts to the HubSpot record (link below).

Next steps:
- Mina will schedule a 30-minute exec sync for April 9 to walk through the changes and timeline.

If you want a formal postmortem doc we’ll produce one and share the RCA with timelines and telemetry graphs. Again — apologies for the disruption and we appreciate your collaboration on the recovery.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
